newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-S.AFRICA CLOSE IN ON TEST, SERIES VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-S.AFRICA CLOSE IN ON TEST, SERIES VICTORY.

text.p: India were left needing a second monumental innings from skipper Sachin Tendulkar after being plunged deep into trouble by South Africa on the fourth day of the second test in Cape Town on Sunday.
Tendulkar, who made a brilliant 169 in India's first innings to ensure that they avoided the follow-on, was undefeated on six at the close as India struggled to 52 for three.
India needed to bat all day on Monday to avoid a second defeat or, more improbably, score another 375 runs to level the three test series after their 328-run defeat in Durban.
South Africa were denied in similar circumstances last season when England skipper Mike Atherton batted for more than five sessions to avert a loss in Johannesburg with an undefeated 185.
India were set 427 for victory from a minimum of 118 overs after South Africa again dominated the day's play, declaring their second innings on 256 for six three overs after tea.
In the 28 overs to be faced India were again quickly in trouble. In the seventh over Allan Donald beat Nayan Mongia to knock back the opener's off-stump for two.

In the 17th over Woorkeri Raman got a thin edge to Shaun Pollock to give a diving catch to keeper Dave Richardson and Tendulkar was brought out at 44 for three four overs later when Paul Adams struck.
Rahul Dravid nibbled at Adams' chinaman as it fizzed down the leg side to give a second catch to the wicketkeeper.
South Africa's total was founded on two more record partnerships -- the sixth and seventh to be posted in the match.

Andrew Hudson and Daryll Cullinan put on 94 for the fourth wicket (beating the 82 of Kepler Wessels and Jonty Rhodes set in Durban four years ago) and Brian McMillan and Shaun Pollock added 101 in an unbroken seventh wicket stand. That surpassed the 8 posted by McMillan and Dave Richardson in the first innings of this match.
South Africa had resumed on 24 for two but quickly lost nightwatchman Lance Klusener who was caught at a shortish midwicket aiming a pull at Javagal Srinath.
Cullinan, walking out at 33 for three, immediately cut his first ball for four and added another five as he went to his second half century of the match in just 71 balls.
Hudson, not out seven overnight, had necessarily been more circumspect and followed the Transvaaler to 50, taking 114 balls and striking seven fours.

They were both dismissed within seven runs of each other shortly after lunch as they looked to force the pace. Cullinan, tied down as leg spinner Anil Kumble bowled outside leg stump from around the wicket, was bowled by a leg spinner as he stepped awy to the on-side.

Hudson chopped on as he attempted to cut Srinath to make it 133 for five and it became 155 for six when Hansie Cronje was well caught by a diving Rahul Dravid at short leg off the bowling of Kumble for 18.
That brought in Pollock to partner McMillan and the pair kept the momentum going as 126 runs were scored between lunch and tea.

They posted their century partnership in just 87 minutes with McMillan following up his first innings century with an undefeated 59 to take his aggregate for the series to 247 for once out. In the series between these sides in India at the end of 1996he had failed to reach 20 in six innings.
Pollock improved his test best score to 40 not out before Cronje declared three overs after tea.
The third test is in Johannesburg from January 16-20.
